The '''1704 [[FLLA]] World Cup''' was the 9th edition of the [[FLLA World Cup]], the quadrennial international [[Arraby]] tournament contested by the senior men's national teams of the member associations of the [[FLLA]]. It was held in [[Emara]] across [[Ayuma]], and was won by [[Emara]], who defeated [[Siana]] 3-2 in the final.

The 1704 edition returned the tournament to [[Ayuma]] after the [[1700 FLLA World Cup|inaugural World Cup]] in [[Atirha]]. [[Emara]] hosted and won on home soil, defeating [[Siana]] 3-2 in the final. The competition is remembered for the technical quality of its closing stages and for the Emaran side's defence of an early lead, an achievement frequently revisited in subsequent FLLA literature as the establishment of the modern Emaran Arraby tradition.
